The source's own published macros arbitrate: our 484 cal / 26.8 P / 34.7 F vs their 452.5 / 23.7 / 35.1 - calories +7%, fat -1%, protein +13% (inside the 15% instrument); the skinless-canon alternative computes 320 cal / -29% - refuted by the source's own label. new_commodity_proposals.proposal: REGISTRAR/GATE REVIEW REQUESTED, not a new commodity: this mapping books bone-in purchase grams against a NEW bone-in-basis DB row (USDA 05091 x 0.80 disclosed yield), departing from the skin-REMOVED canon ruling ('the estate's answer is the substitution, not a bone-in DB row' - burmese-chicken-dal-curry). That ruling's own rationale (bone-in grams corrupt MEAT-basis macros) does not bite here because the row is bone-in-basis by construction, and the skinless rebuild it prescribes would drop this in-band skin-on braise ~130 cal/serving below the run's 400 floor while misstating fat ~2x. Asking for the ruling to be scoped to skin-removed sources; if the registrar rules the other way, this recipe re-books to BSCT and retires at the band gate honestly.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS: protein +13.1% (inside the 15% instrument), calories +7.0%, fat -1.1% (near-exact - and fat is the skin-sensitive number, validating the skin-on basis). The rejected alternative (skinless BSCT rebuild per canon) computes ~320 cal / 20.8 P - calories -29% vs the source's own label and below the run floor - so the source label refutes the skinless reading, not ours. Carbs +47% relative but +3.1 g absolute (9.7 vs 6.6), driven by onion/tomato rounding; irrelevant against the 35 g ceiling.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 484.2 cal in [400, 650] PASS (84 above the floor, 166 of ceiling headroom); carbs 9.7 g <= 35 PASS. Bacon-row raw-vs-cooked ambiguity (see line note) spreads the estimate ~454-484; both ends in band.
